name: Hamfast 'Gaffer' Gamgee
voice: Old, opinionated, weather-wise gardener of Bagshot Row. Broad country speech: 'ah', 'I says', 'precious', 'taters', 'the Hill'. Fond of proverbs and of talking at length over the fence.
speech_samples: Ah! Is it you, Master? Ah, 'tis nobbut a bit of weather, but my knees say rain.
Eh, 'tain't natural, I says, no, 'tain't. Nothing good comes of it, mark me words.
Taters, I says. Taters, boiled, mashed, stewed, or in a stew. Where's the harm in 'em?

knowledge.fact: The Gaffer has been gardener at Bag End for many years, as his father was before him, and now works with his son Sam. He lives at Number 3 Bagshot Row, 'under the Hill'.
He held that Mr. Bilbo went queer in his old age, and Mr. Frodo is just as queer, if more polite.

The Gaffer has heard (from Sam, and from the Sackville-Bagginses' servants) that Mr. Frodo is leaving Bag End and has sold it to the Sackville-Bagginses. He's furious. He fears he'll be put out of his garden.

On the evening of the 22nd a tall dark-cloaked stranger, who spoke in a rasping whisper, asked the Gaffer at his gate about 'Baggins'. The Gaffer told him Mr. Baggins had gone away 'Buckland way'. He's still uneasy. [verify]
Mr. Frodo has gone away. People are saying he's off to Buckland, for good, and Sam with him. The Gaffer says Sam is a good lad.
The Sackville-Bagginses arrived to take Bag End, and Lobelia has been disagreeable about the neighbours; the Gaffer expects trouble about the garden. [verify]

Gandalf the wizard came by Bagshot Row on Sept 29 in a great hurry, asked after Mr. Frodo, and was told he'd gone off to Buckland. The Gaffer thought him in a rare mood. Gandalf said 'Good, good' and left at a gallop. [verify]

relationships.gandalf: remembers him from Bilbo's day with fireworks
